scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request states that dispute tickets roughly doubled since August.

hypotheses.statement: The requester frames the surge in dispute tickets as a response-speed problem solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and corrects underlying bill errors.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, deploying an AI agent would address the issue; if false, other root causes must be addressed.

hypotheses.statement: AMI read events from MDMS are delayed, missing, or corrupted, leading to estimation or incorrect bills that drive dispute tickets.
hypotheses.rationale: If MDMS data quality is the cause, fixing the data pipeline (or using alternative reads) would reduce tickets; an AI agent would only treat symptoms.

hypotheses.statement: Manual meter reads from field services are incomplete, inaccurate, or not uploaded correctly, causing estimation substitution and wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If field read problems dominate, improving field processes or handoff fidelity would cut tickets; an AI agent would not fix the source.

hypotheses.statement: A recent change to billing import validation rules (since August) introduced logic that misapplies tariffs or read types, producing incorrect bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If a rule change is at fault, reverting or correcting the rule would resolve the issue; an AI agent would not address the rule defect.

hypotheses.statement: The handoff of field manual reads (H-FIELD-BILL) or MDMS reads (H-MDMS-BILL) suffers from latency, format errors, or missing data, causing the billing system to fallback to estimates and generate wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If handoff issues are primary, improving the handoff mechanisms would reduce tickets; an AI agent would only mitigate the symptom.
